question: A CDL is required to operate a single commercial vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of:
explanation: The manual states a CDL is required to operate 'Any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 26,001 pounds or more.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A CDL is required for a combination vehicle with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) exceeds:
explanation: The manual requires a CDL for a combination vehicle with GCWR of 26,001+ pounds 'provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is in excess of 10,000 pounds.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A CDL is required to operate a vehicle designed to transport how many or more passengers, including the driver?
explanation: The manual lists 'A vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers (including the driver)' among the vehicles requiring a CDL.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: Regardless of size, a CDL is also required for any vehicle that:
choice_b: Tows a trailer under 10,000 pounds GVWR
choice_c: Is used only for personal use
choice_d: Requires hazardous material placards or carries a select agent/toxin listed in 42 CFR part 73
explanation: The manual states a CDL is required for 'Any size vehicle which requires hazardous material placards or is carrying material listed as a select agent or toxin in 42 CFR part 73.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A driver holding a Class A CDL may also legally drive vehicles in which other class(es)?
choice_a: Both Class B and Class C
choice_d: Neither Class B nor Class C
explanation: Since Class A skills include those required for B and C vehicles, 'a driver who has a Class A license also may drive vehicles in Classes B and C.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: Vehicles with a GVWR under 26,001 pounds (Class C) fall under the CDL program only if they are:
choice_a: Registered under the International Registration Plan
choice_b: Designed to carry 16 or more passengers, or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding
explanation: The manual limits Class C CDL coverage to vehicles '(1) Designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or (2) Used to transport hazardous materials in quantities requiring placarding.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: How many kinds of CDL endorsements does the manual describe that may be required depending on the vehicle or cargo?
explanation: The manual states 'There are six kinds of CDL endorsements that may be required, depending on the vehicle or type of cargo.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_d: Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N)
explanation: The manual notes 'The only endorsements that may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) are: Passenger (P); School bus (S); and Tank vehicle (N).'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required for tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of at least:
explanation: The endorsement applies to tanks 'having an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Before pulling double or triple trailers, a Class A driver must:
choice_b: Pass a special knowledge examination on the problems associated with pulling multiple trailers
choice_c: Obtain a hazardous materials endorsement first
explanation: The manual states 'A special knowledge examination on the problems associated with pulling multiple trailers must be passed' to add the Doubles/Triples (T) endorsement.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: In addition to a special written examination, what else is required to obtain a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement?
explanation: The manual states the TSA and US DOT 'require background checks on commercial drivers who are certified to transport hazardous materials.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: How many standardized restriction codes does the manual identify?
explanation: The manual states 'There are ten standardized restriction codes.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A CDL holder receives an 'E' restriction (No manual transmission) when the skills test is performed in a vehicle equipped with:
explanation: If the skills test is performed 'in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission,' the CDL must show the person is restricted from operating a CMV with a manual transmission.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: The 'K' restriction on a CDL limits the driver to:
explanation: '(K) - Intrastate only' means the driver is 'restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: An applicant receives an 'L' restriction (No air brake equipped CMV) if they:
choice_c: Do not take or fail the air brake component of the knowledge test, or test in a vehicle not equipped with air brakes
explanation: The 'L' restriction applies 'if an applicant does not take or fails the air brake component of the knowledge test, or performs the skills test in a vehicle not equipped with air brakes.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: The CDL Skills Test consists of three segments that must be taken and passed, in order, as:
choice_a: On-road driving, vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control
choice_b: Basic vehicle control, on-road driving, vehicle inspection
choice_c: Vehicle inspection, on-road driving, basic vehicle control
choice_d: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving
explanation: The manual states the Skills Test consists of 'Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving. You must take the segments in the order listed and must pass each one before moving to the next.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: A court may fine a driver up to how much for holding more than one driver's license?
explanation: The manual states 'You cannot have more than one license. If you break this rule, a court may fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-9

question: It is illegal to operate a CMV if the driver's blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is:
explanation: The manual states 'It is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is .04% or more.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: For a first offense such as driving a CMV with a BAC of .04% or higher, a driver loses their CDL for at least:
explanation: The manual states 'You will lose your CDL for at least one year for a first offense' including driving with a BAC of .04% or higher.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: The minimum CDL disqualification increases to three years for a first offense (such as a BAC of .04%+) if it occurs while operating a CMV that is:
explanation: The manual states 'You will lose your CDL for at least three years if the offense occurs while you are operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: What is the penalty for a second disqualifying offense (such as a second DUI in a CMV)?
explanation: The manual states 'You will lose your CDL for life for a second offense.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: A driver found to have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% BAC will be:
choice_d: Required to retake the knowledge test
explanation: The manual states 'You will be put out-of-service for 24 hours if you have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04%.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: Under the manual's definition, 'excessive speeding' as a serious traffic violation means driving:
choice_a: 5 mph or more above the posted limit
choice_b: 10 mph or more above the posted limit
choice_c: 20 mph or more above the posted limit
choice_d: 15 mph or more above the posted limit
explanation: The manual defines serious traffic violations as including 'excessive speeding (15 mph or more above the posted limit).'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: A driver who commits two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: The manual states the driver loses their CDL 'For at least 60 days if you have committed two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What is the minimum CDL disqualification for a first violation of an out-of-service order?
explanation: The manual states a driver loses their CDL 'For at least 90 days if you have committed your first violation of an out-of-service order.'
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8
